Independent gap, kernel derivative, angular endpoint, and integration estimates
correctness.rationale: Writing r=|1−z|, ρ=1−|z|², p=α+2 and κ=1−c gives the exact gap R=1−|φ(z)|²=c(ρ+κr²). The perturbation changes this by at most (4|ε|c²+16|ε|²c⁴)r², strictly below cκr², so the disk self-maps are uniformly inside the disk away from contact. Standard boundedness of composition on the weighted Bergman disk and boundedness of the multiplier give a bounded D. Tonelli and Parseval give its extended squared kernel energy. Along the symbol segment the gap is comparable to R; the first kernel derivative has squared norm asymptotic p(p+1)R^(−p−2), and the second derivative has Hilbert-space norm O(R^(−(p+4)/2)) by mixed differentiation of the reproducing kernel. Taylor's relative error is O(|δ|/R)=O(r^(γ−2)) uniformly, which is decisive at tangential approaches. Each angular arc contributes Jacobian r/(2√(1−r²(v+1)²/4)) at v=ρ/r². The angular weight v^α/(v+κ)^(α+4) has integrable error O(r²)(v+1)² times the weight up to v=1/r; the remaining singular endpoint has total O(r³). The slice integral is continuous at each 0<r<2 by setting v=u(2/r−1), with local domination by u^α(1−u)^(−1/2). The limiting integral κ^(−3)B(α+1,3) cancels the factors (α+1)p(p+1), giving 2|ε|²c^(2γ−α−4)/(πκ³) as the coefficient of r^(2s−6). It also gives the stated normalized angular law, with equal limiting arc masses even for complex ε. Integrating gives the power and logarithm, exactly s>5/2 for membership, and residue 𝒜/2 from ∫₀^r₀ r^(2(s−5/2)−1)dr. The error bound is uniform as β approaches the stated pole with 2<γ<5/2 fixed, because the β weight is constant on a slice.
residual_risks: The recorded finite quadrature uses only real perturbations. The complex case and the full parameter range follow from the uniform analytic bounds, not the quadrature. No assertion is extended to γ=2.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The necessity and exact refinements are not a parameter substitution into the inspected statements; they require the uniform kernel expansion and evaluation of the dominant angular layer. The numerical threshold value in the earlier sufficient statement is not itself credited as a new constant.

evidence: The Bergman example takes φ=az+1−a, ψ=φ+ε(1−φ)^b, u=v=z. This is the same family at β=0 with a=c, b=γ, restricted a and positive ε. The Hardy example is closely related, in H². The earlier beta-prime theorem is for a matrix column/row energy ratio with parameters (α+2,−α), not the angular variable v on shrinking circles with scaled (α+1,3) law.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Treat the prior contact ansatz and the β=0 overlap explicitly; do not identify Hardy with weighted Bergman or the matrix ratio with the angular slice, which have different measures and observables.
